title: 12 Days: Solomon Northup and Albert Camus

sentences.en: Hello, welcome to The Rest is History.
sentences.zh: 你好，欢迎收听《历史的余烬》。

sentences.en: It is the 4th of January, and we are ploughing through the 12 days of Christmas.
sentences.zh: 今天是1月4日，我们正在经历圣诞节的最后几天。

sentences.en: As you can probably tell, the sheer pressure of recording all these 12 days of Christmas podcasts has led to me partially losing my voice.
sentences.zh: 如你所见，录制这些圣诞节播客的巨大压力导致我的声音有点哑了。

sentences.en: But that's fine, because Tom Holland loves to talk.
sentences.zh: 不过没关系，因为汤姆·霍兰德喜欢聊天。

sentences.en: No, but my voice is going as well.
sentences.zh: 不，不过我的声音也快哑了。

sentences.en: Oh no, Tom, the Jeopardy.
sentences.zh: 噢不，汤姆，别这样。

sentences.en: It's a sexy husk.
sentences.zh: 听起来带着一种性感的沙哑。

sentences.en: Well, yes.
sentences.zh: 好吧，是的。

sentences.en: Like Margaret Thatcher's voice, is that what you mean?
sentences.zh: 就像玛格丽特·撒切尔的声音，你是这个意思吗？

sentences.en: Yes, very, very like that.
sentences.zh: 对，非常、非常像那样。

sentences.en: Very like Mrs Thatcher.
sentences.zh: 非常像撒切尔夫人。

sentences.en: I'm going very, very, very, very, very rough voice.
sentences.zh: 我的声音变得非常、非常、非常、非常、非常粗糙。

sentences.en: Tom, I think you've been doing splendidly.
sentences.zh: 汤姆，我觉得你表现得很棒。

sentences.en: You've been doing wonderfully well.
sentences.zh: 你表现得好极了。

sentences.en: Thank you.
sentences.zh: 谢谢。

sentences.en: I'm very pleased with you.
sentences.zh: 我对你非常满意。

sentences.en: Thank you.
sentences.zh: 谢谢。

sentences.en: Would you give us, please, your events that happen on this day in history, and make it a good one, Tom?
sentences.zh: 请跟我们讲讲历史上这一天发生了什么事吧，讲个精彩的，汤姆？

sentences.en: Yeah, so today is, it's the day that Solomon Northrup regained his freedom, January the 4th, 1853.
sentences.zh: 好的，所以今天，也就是所罗门·诺瑟普重获自由的日子，1853年1月4日。

sentences.en: And Solomon Northrup will be familiar to anyone who has seen Steve McQueen's Oscar-winning film,
sentences.zh: 看过史蒂夫·麦奎因获得奥斯卡奖的电影的人，都会对所罗门·诺瑟普感到熟悉，

sentences.en: 12 Years a Slave.
sentences.zh: 《为奴十二年》。

sentences.en: So, this is the terrible story of a black man born in New York State, freeborn.
sentences.zh: 所以，这是一个可怕的故事，一个在纽约州出生的黑人，生而自由。

sentences.en: He's a farmer.
sentences.zh: 他是一名农民。

sentences.en: He was also a very proficient violinist, and this was the key to what then happens.
sentences.zh: 他也是一位非常高超的小提琴手，而这正是接下来发生的事情的关键。

sentences.en: He's played by Chiwetel Ejiofor in the film.
sentences.zh: 他在电影中由切瓦特·埃加福特饰演。

sentences.en: And Solomon Northrup, he is, so his mother is a freeborn woman.
sentences.zh: 而所罗门·诺瑟普，他的母亲是一个生而自由的女人。

sentences.en: His father is a freed slave.
sentences.zh: 他的父亲是一个获得自由的奴隶。

sentences.en: There's absolutely no question about the fact, you know, he's not, he's not in any way a slave.
sentences.zh: 毫无疑问，你知道的，他根本不是、绝不是什么奴隶。

sentences.en: He's completely a free man.
sentences.zh: 他完全是一个自由人。

sentences.en: He marries a woman called Anne Hampton, who's a kind of mix of black, white, Native American.
sentences.zh: 他娶了一个名叫安·汉普顿的女人，她身上有着黑人、白人和美洲原住民的血统。

sentences.en: And she's a cook.
sentences.zh: 她是一名厨师。

sentences.en: So, they're kind of, they're, I guess, kind of, they're kind of lower class, but they're, you know, they're not on the breadline at all.
sentences.zh: 所以他们有点，我猜，属于下层阶级，但他们，你知道的，绝对没有到山穷水尽的地步。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: And they have, they're very happily married.
sentences.zh: 而且他们的婚姻非常幸福。

sentences.en: And in 1841, because, as I mentioned, he has this proficiency at the violin, he's offered us a job as a musician in Washington, D.C.
sentences.zh: 而在1841年，正如我所提到的，因为他小提琴拉得很好，有人提供给他一份在华盛顿特区当音乐家的工作。

sentences.en: And Washington, D.C., of course, is that much further south.
sentences.zh: 而华盛顿特区，当然，要往南得多。

sentences.en: Of course.
sentences.zh: 当然。

sentences.en: Than New York.
sentences.zh: 比纽约更南。

sentences.en: And so, therefore, closer to the line where slaves, where slavery is still legal.
sentences.zh: 因此，也就更靠近奴隶制仍然合法的地区。

sentences.en: Well, they have big slave markets, I think, in Washington, don't they?
sentences.zh: 我想，华盛顿有很大的奴隶市场吧？

sentences.en: And basically, it turns out that the people who've offered Solomon Northrup this job are, they're crooks.
sentences.zh: 基本上，事实证明，给所罗门·诺瑟普提供这份工作的人是一群骗子。

sentences.en: And they've ordered him because they want to sell him as a slave.
sentences.zh: 他们把他诱骗来是因为想把他当奴隶卖掉。

sentences.en: So, they get him to Washington, D.C.
sentences.zh: 所以他们把他带到了华盛顿特区。

sentences.en: under this false prospectus.
sentences.zh: 用的就是这个虚假的幌子。

sentences.en: They drug him.
sentences.zh: 他们给他下药。

sentences.en: They kidnap him.
sentences.zh: 他们绑架了他。

sentences.en: They sell him.
sentences.zh: 他们把他卖了。

sentences.en: And he gets shipped to New Orleans.
sentences.zh: 然后他被运到了新奥尔良。

sentences.en: And you can imagine, it's just, I mean, the most terrible thing to happen.
sentences.zh: 你可以想象，这简直是，我是说，最可怕的遭遇了。

sentences.en: And in New Orleans, he is bought by Benedict Cumberbatch.
sentences.zh: 在新奥尔良，他被本尼迪克特·康伯巴奇买下了。

sentences.en: So, William Prince Ford, who is a Baptist minister.
sentences.zh: 也就是威廉·普林斯·福特，他是一位浸信会牧师。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: And Baptists generally, you know, certainly in the north, they're very kind of abolitionists.
sentences.zh: 一般来说，浸信会教徒，你知道的，当然在北方，他们非常倾向于废奴主义。

sentences.en: They're very much at the kind of the front line of opposing slavery.
sentences.zh: 他们基本上站在反对奴隶制的最前线。

sentences.en: And Ford is a troubled slave owner, I think it would be fair to say.
sentences.zh: 我觉得可以说，福特是一个内心纠结的奴隶主。

sentences.en: And in due course, when Northrup writes up his memoirs, 12 Years a Slave, he writes of William Ford, in my opinion, there never was a more kind, noble,
sentences.zh: 随后，当诺瑟普写下他的回忆录《为奴十二年》时，他这样评价威廉·福特：“依我之见，从未有过比威廉·福特更善良、更高尚、更坦诚的基督徒了。”

sentences.en: candid Christian man than William Ford.
sentences.zh: “一直包围着他的环境和交往，使他盲目地看不到奴隶制体系根基中固有的错误。”

sentences.en: The influences and associations that had always surrounded him, blinded him to the inherent wrong at the bottom of the system of slavery.
sentences.zh: 从我们的角度来看，对于一个人来说，这两句话真的是太惊人了。

sentences.en: It's kind of, from our perspective, an amazing couple of sentences for someone to write.
sentences.zh: 这会显得非常宽容，对吧。

sentences.en: It's going to be very gracious, yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的，但是，我的意义在于，它让人深刻意识到废奴主义所依托的那些假设是多么激进的一场颠覆。

sentences.en: Yeah, but, I mean, I think it brings home just how radical and upheaval the kind of, the assumptions that come to underpin abolitionism are.
sentences.zh: 人们把奴隶制度视为理所当然，竟然持续了这么久。

sentences.en: That people had taken the institution of slavery for granted for so long.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 以至于完全可以一边接受一个人是个善良、高尚、坦诚的基督徒，一边还觉得奴隶制没问题。

sentences.en: That it was perfectly possible to accept that a man could be a kind, noble, candid Christian man and still think that slavery was fine.
sentences.zh: 是的，当然。

sentences.en: Yeah, of course.
sentences.zh: 是的，我的意思是，这是一个巨大的主题，我想我们会在某个时候做一个关于奴隶制的节目。

sentences.en: Yeah, I mean, it's a huge theme that, I think we're going to do an episode on slavery at some point.
sentences.zh: 你会毫不意外地发现，我的确认为废奴主义的源泉深深植根于基督教。

sentences.en: And it won't surprise you to know that I do think that the wellsprings of abolitionism are deeply Christian.
sentences.zh: 哦，汤姆，我想在这方面你并不孤单。

sentences.en: Oh, Tom, I don't think you're alone in that way.
sentences.zh: 我是说，在你的所有观点中，这大概是最不具争议的一个了。

sentences.en: I mean, that's hardly, of all your views, that's probably the least controversial.
sentences.zh: 但是，显而易见，基督教的论点也被用来为奴隶制辩护。

sentences.en: But, obviously, Christian arguments are also used to justify slavery.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 所以，这个人物，你知道的，这位浸信会牧师因为这个原因是一个挺有趣的人物。

sentences.en: And so, this figure, you know, this Baptist minister is kind of an interesting figure for that reason.
sentences.zh: 接下来发生的事情是，福特陷入了财务困境。

sentences.en: So, what then happens is that Ford gets into financial difficulties.
sentences.zh: 于是他把诺瑟普转手卖给了一个名叫约翰·蒂博的木匠，而这个人，他是个混蛋。

sentences.en: And so, he sells Northrop on to this carpenter called John Thibault, who is, he's a wanker.
sentences.zh: 我能说吗？我用了那个词，对吧？

sentences.en: Am I allowed to, I used that word, didn't I?
sentences.zh: 就像那个从你车里偷走火鸡的家伙。

sentences.en: It's like the guy who stole the turkey out of your car.
sentences.zh: 我觉得他可能比那个还要糟。

sentences.en: I think he's probably even worse than that.
sentences.zh: 还要糟，我的天哪。

sentences.en: Even worse, my word.
sentences.zh: 比那还要糟。

sentences.en: Even worse than that.
sentences.zh: 而蒂博，我是说，他绝对是个畜生。

sentences.en: And Thibault is, I mean, he's an absolute brute.
sentences.zh: 他差点私刑处死诺瑟普。

sentences.en: He almost lynches Northrop.
sentences.zh: 但他们打了一架什么的，对吧？

sentences.en: But they have a fight or something, don't they?
sentences.zh: 他们打了一架，是的。

sentences.en: They have a fight, yeah.
sentences.zh: 但福特来了，把诺瑟普救了下来。

sentences.en: But Ford comes, cuts Northrop down.
sentences.zh: 所以他在那里扮演了好人的角色。

sentences.en: So, he's kind of playing the good guy there.
sentences.zh: 然后，蒂博又把他转手卖给了一个名叫埃德温·埃普斯的种植园主。

sentences.en: And then, Thibault sells him on to a plantation owner called Edwin Epps.
sentences.zh: 在电影中，他由迈克尔·法斯宾德饰演。

sentences.en: And in the film, he's played by Michael Fassbender.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，迈克尔·法斯宾德总是饰演那种你绝对不想被卖给他当奴隶的角色。

sentences.en: I mean, Michael Fassbender always plays the kind of character you don't want to be sold to as a slave.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 他演过麦克白，对吧？

sentences.en: He played Mabeth, didn't he?
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 没错，他演过。

sentences.en: Yeah, he did.
sentences.zh: 他还演过万磁王，我想是在《X战警》里。

sentences.en: And he played Magneto, I think, in The X-Men.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 我知道你是超级英雄的超级粉丝，汤姆。

sentences.en: I know you're a big superheroes fan, Tom.
sentences.zh: 好吧，那些就是我喜欢的。

sentences.en: Well, so those are the ones that I liked.
sentences.zh: 那些是我看过的。

sentences.en: Those are the ones I saw.
sentences.zh: 对。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 所以，迈克尔·法斯宾德演的是年轻的，那谁演年老的？

sentences.en: So, Michael Fassbender plays the young, who plays the older one?
sentences.zh: 老年的万磁王。

sentences.en: The old Magneto.
sentences.zh: 是伊恩·麦克莱恩还是帕特里克·斯图尔特？

sentences.en: Is it Ian McKellen or Patrick Stewart?
sentences.zh: 是的，是伊恩·麦克莱恩。

sentences.en: Yes, it's Ian McKellen.
sentences.zh: 没错，是伊恩·麦克莱恩。

sentences.en: Yes, it's Ian McKellen.
sentences.zh: 对的。

sentences.en: That's right.
sentences.zh: 所以，无论如何，他，这个可怜的家伙，诺瑟普，所罗门·诺瑟普，去到了路易斯安那州，在《为奴十二年》中作为奴隶劳作。

sentences.en: So, anyway, so he, this poor guy, Northrop, Solomon Northrop, goes to, he has to work as a slave in Louisiana and 12 years a slave.
sentences.zh: 他就在那里辛苦劳作。

sentences.en: And there he is, toiling away.
sentences.zh: 第十二年的时候，他遇到了一个在种植园工作的加拿大人，一个叫塞缪尔·巴斯的人。

sentences.en: 12 years in, he meets a Canadian who's working on the plantation, a guy called Samuel Bass.
sentences.zh: 而塞缪尔·巴斯把消息传回了纽约。

sentences.en: And Samuel Bass gets word back to New York.
sentences.zh: 巴斯是个废奴主义者，是这样吗？

sentences.en: Bass is an abolitionist, is that right?
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: Yes.
sentences.zh: 而且，你知道的，他这么做需要很大的勇气，因为他这么做违反了南方的法律。

sentences.en: And it's, you know, it's a brave thing for him to do because he's breaking Southern law by doing that.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 路易斯安那州的法律。

sentences.en: Louisiana law.
sentences.zh: 但在纽约，州法律规定要向被绑架和奴役的纽约自由公民提供援助。

sentences.en: But in New York, the law of the state provides aid to free New York citizens who've been kidnapped and enslaved.
sentences.zh: 所以这显然是一件规模很大的事。

sentences.en: So, it's obviously a kind of massive thing that's going on.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，这种事发生得太频繁了，以至于各州都有应对它的条款。

sentences.en: I mean, it's happening so often that there are state provisions to combat it.
sentences.zh: 因此，诺瑟普的家人，以及一直对忠于他的妻子安·汉普顿……

sentences.en: And so, Northrop's family and his wife, Anne Hampton, has stayed true to him.
sentences.zh: 所罗门·诺瑟普也一直对安保持着忠贞的爱情。

sentences.en: Solomon Northrop has stayed true in his love to Anne.
sentences.zh: 所以，我的意思是，这是一个非常感人的故事。

sentences.en: So, I mean, that's kind of a very touching story.
sentences.zh: 很暖心，是的。

sentences.en: Heartwarming, yeah.
sentences.zh: 所以，诺瑟普的家人和朋友寻求了纽约州长华盛顿·亨特的帮助。

sentences.en: So, Northrop's family and friends, they enlist the aid of the governor of New York, a guy called Washington Hunt.
sentences.zh: 诺瑟普于1853年的这一天重获自由。

sentences.en: And Northrop gains his freedom on this day in 1853.
sentences.zh: 而他的绑架者，你知道的，什么事也没有。

sentences.en: And his kidnappers, you know, nothing happens to them.
sentences.zh: 他们从未受到惩罚。

sentences.en: They never get punished.
sentences.zh: 他们从未被抓到。

sentences.en: They never get caught.
sentences.zh: 对，我想追踪他们大概很难吧。

sentences.en: Yeah, probably quite hard to track them down, I suppose.
sentences.zh: 那年晚些时候，有人鼓励他写下所发生的事情的经过。

sentences.en: Later in the year, he gets encouraged to write up the story of what's happened.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 因此，《为奴十二年》成了废奴运动中非常重要的文本。

sentences.en: And so, 12 Years a Slave, it becomes very significant text in the abolitionist cause.
sentences.zh: 而且诺瑟普，我是说，他为此做了相当多的宣传活动。

sentences.en: And Northrop, I mean, he does quite a lot of campaigning on it.
sentences.zh: 然后他就渐渐淡出了公众记录。

sentences.en: And then he just kind of fades from the record.
sentences.zh: 我们知道他后来怎么了吗？

sentences.en: And do we know what happened to him?
sentences.zh: 不太清楚，没有。

sentences.en: Not really, no.
sentences.zh: 但我想这本书就是他的纪念碑，对吧？

sentences.en: But I suppose the book is his memorial, isn't it?
sentences.zh: 这本书和这部电影。

sentences.en: The book and the film.
sentences.zh: 对，这本书和电影。

sentences.en: Yeah, the book and the film.
sentences.zh: 因为这本书是奴隶叙事文学的一种。

sentences.en: Because the book is one of those slave narratives.
sentences.zh: 这类叙事作品在内战爆发前的几年里，在唤醒北方民众的心灵和灵魂方面发挥了巨大的作用，不是吗？

sentences.en: That those sort of narratives play a huge part in kind of rousing the hearts and souls of kind of northern opinion in the years before the Civil War, don't they?
sentences.zh: 《汤姆叔叔的小屋》那一类型的。

sentences.en: Uncle Tom's cabin type.
sentences.zh: 我是说，《汤姆叔叔的小屋》显然略有不同。

sentences.en: I mean, Uncle Tom's cabin is obviously slightly different.
sentences.zh: 但逃亡奴隶的这类故事，以及其中的恐怖和不公，比起任何政治宣传册，更能让那些没有政治倾向、不属于任何党派的普通人深刻感受到制度的残酷，你觉得呢？

sentences.en: But those sort of stories of fugitive slaves and sort of the horrors and the sort of the injustice of it, they bring home probably more than any number of tracts,
sentences.zh: 嗯，我也认为这有着特殊的震撼力，显然，大多数废奴叙事都是面向白人废奴主义者的，特别是在北方。

sentences.en: non-political kind of unaffiliated people, just the horror of the institution, don't you think?
sentences.zh: 它本质上是在说，怜悯那些可怜的黑人吧，可怜的黑奴。

sentences.en: Well, I think also the particular impact of this is, I mean, obviously, most of the narratives, the abolitionist narratives, are for white abolitionists, particularly in the North.
sentences.zh: 但对北方的白人来说，要他们把自己想象成黑奴仍然是非常、非常困难的。

sentences.en: It's essentially saying, you know, pity the poor black people, the poor black slaves.
sentences.zh: 但这力量的源泉在于，因为所罗门·诺瑟普原本是北方州的一个自由人，

sentences.en: But they're still, you know, it's very, very difficult for white people in the North to imagine themselves as black slaves.
sentences.zh: 因此，北方的白人就更容易设身处地去感受他的处境。

sentences.en: But the power of this is that because Solomon Northrup was a free man in a northern state,
sentences.zh: 我想这就是它的力量所在。

sentences.en: it therefore becomes much easier for white people in the North to put themselves into his shoes.
sentences.zh: 因为对诺瑟普而言，最震撼的并不是他生为奴隶，或是被从非洲贩卖为奴。

sentences.en: And I think that's the power of it.
sentences.zh: 这就是它的力量所在。

sentences.en: Because the shock for Northrup isn't that he's been born into slavery or he's been brought from Africa into slavery.
sentences.zh: 因为对诺瑟普而言，最震撼的并不是他生为奴隶，或是被从非洲贩卖为奴。

sentences.en: He's someone who was born free, who's lived free, and who then becomes a slave.
sentences.zh: 他生而自由，一生自由，最终却沦为奴隶。

sentences.en: And I think that, you know, just kind of emotionally, perhaps, for white readers in the northern states, it makes the horror of what happened to him all the greater.
sentences.zh: 我认为，你知道的，从某种情感层面来说，对北方各州的白人读者而言，这让发生在他身上的恐怖遭遇显得更加惨烈。

sentences.en: That's a good story.
sentences.zh: 这是个好故事。

sentences.en: It's a fascinating story.
sentences.zh: 这是一个引人入胜的故事。

sentences.en: It reminds me a tiny, I mean, I'll tell you a narrative from a century later that has always stuck in my mind.
sentences.zh: 它让我想起了一点，我是说，我跟你讲一个来自一个世纪后的故事，它一直留在我的脑海里。

sentences.en: You may not have read it.
sentences.zh: 你可能没读过。

sentences.en: It's a book called Black Like Me by John Howard Griffin.
sentences.zh: 这是一本叫《我如黑人》的书，作者是约翰·霍华德·格里芬。

sentences.en: Have you ever read that?
sentences.zh: 你读过那本吗？

sentences.en: No, I haven't.
sentences.zh: 不，我没读过。

sentences.en: So this is, again, a book very powerful with white audiences.
sentences.zh: 所以这也是一本对白人读者极具震撼力的书。

sentences.en: But the difference here is it's not that Griffin was free and became a slave.
sentences.zh: 但这里的区别在于，并不是格里芬本来是自由的然后变成了奴隶。

sentences.en: It was white and then he literally blacked up.
sentences.zh: 而是他是白人，然后他真的把自己涂黑了。

sentences.en: So he decided, so it's sort of in the middle of the civil rights movement.
sentences.zh: 所以他决定，这大约发生在民权运动中期。

sentences.en: And he, I think it was the 50s.
sentences.zh: 而且他，我想那是50年代。

sentences.en: He decides, he goes to a doctor's friend, a doctor friend and a dermatologiSt.
sentences.zh: 他决定去拜访一个医生朋友，一个医生朋友兼皮肤科医生。

sentences.en: And he says, basically, make me black.
sentences.zh: 他对他们说，基本上，把我变成黑人。

sentences.en: And they give him this sort of, they give him drugs.
sentences.zh: 然后他们给了他这种，他们给他开了药。

sentences.en: And then he has hours and hours every day under a lamp to sort of darken his skin.
sentences.zh: 然后他每天花好几个小时在灯光下照射，好把皮肤弄黑。

sentences.en: And then he puts on a stain on top of it.
sentences.zh: 接着他在上面涂了一层着色剂。

sentences.en: And then he basically spends, I think, something like six weeks, maybe longer,
sentences.zh: 然后基本上，我想他花了大约六周时间，也许更长，

sentences.en: traveling through the south and describing as a white man what it's like to be treated as a black man.
sentences.zh: 以一个白人的身份游历南方，去体验并描述被当成黑人对待是什么感觉。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是啊。

sentences.en: And again, it's the kind of story that actually, because he's not black, because he's white,
sentences.zh: 而且同样，这种故事之所以能起作用，是因为他不是黑人，因为他是白人，

sentences.en: that kind of gives him an in with readers who might have just dismissed the book and not, you know.
sentences.zh: 这种身份让他更容易被那些原本可能对这本书不屑一顾、你知道的读者所接受。

sentences.en: And he just sort of talks about what an unbelievable, what an eye opening.
sentences.zh: 他只是谈论了那种难以置信的、大开眼界的感觉。

sentences.en: So there is a massive, there is a massive change in how he's treated.
sentences.zh: 所以，他受到的对待发生了巨大的，天翻地覆的变化。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是啊。

sentences.en: It's colossal.
sentences.zh: 简直巨大。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 对。

sentences.en: Of course, well, he's literally sitting in a different part of the bus.
sentences.zh: 当然，他真的得坐在巴士的不同区域了。

sentences.en: And if he can, and his, and instinctively, you know, he'll go to the sort of white seats, counters and things like that.
sentences.zh: 而且如果可以的话，本能地，你知道的，他会走到那种白人专用的座位、柜台之类的地方。

sentences.en: And people glare at him.
sentences.zh: 然后人们怒目而视。

sentences.en: And he realizes, you know, he could be, it's not plausible that he could be killed for being in the wrong place at the wrong time, the wrong look at the wrong woman,
sentences.zh: 他意识到，你知道的，他可能会，在错误的时间出现在错误的地点、对错误的女人投去错误的一瞥，这些都有可能让他丧命，

sentences.en: all that kind of thing.
sentences.zh: 诸如此类的事情。

sentences.en: So that's a little, a very unjolly reading recommendation.
sentences.zh: 所以这是一个，呃，非常不那么欢乐的阅读推荐。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 对。

sentences.en: I mean, 12 Years a Slave.
sentences.zh: 我是说，《为奴十二年》。

sentences.en: Have you, have you read it, Tom?
sentences.zh: 你，你读过吗，汤姆？

sentences.en: I haven't read it.
sentences.zh: 我没读过。

sentences.en: I've seen the film.
sentences.zh: 我看过电影。

sentences.en: I've seen the film.
sentences.zh: 我看过电影。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 对。

sentences.en: I haven't read the book.
sentences.zh: 我没读过书。

sentences.en: But I, but I quite feel quite inspired by, by doing, you know, thinking about this to go and read it.
sentences.zh: 但我，但我相当受启发，通过思考这些，想去读一读。

sentences.en: Well, it's obviously a harrowing read.
sentences.zh: 嗯，这显然是一段揪心的阅读经历。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是啊。

sentences.en: I mean, unbelievably, it's a harrowing story, isn't it?
sentences.zh: 我是说，难以置信，这是一个揪心的故事，对吧？

sentences.en: To go from, you know, you think you're off to playing a circus, violin in the circus, and you end up being beaten on a plantation.
sentences.zh: 从，你知道的，你以为你是去马戏团拉小提琴，结果却在种植园里挨鞭子。

sentences.en: Anyway, rather depressing subject.
sentences.zh: 总之，是个相当令人沮丧的主题。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是啊。

sentences.en: Sorry about that.
sentences.zh: 真是不好意思。

sentences.en: But it's, but it's, but it's difficult, isn't it?
sentences.zh: 但，但，但这也挺难的，不是吗？

sentences.en: I mean, 12 Days of Christmas, ho, ho, ho, jollity, jollity.
sentences.zh: 我是说，《圣诞节的十二天》，哦，哦，哦，欢乐，欢乐。

sentences.en: But I mean, basically things are memorable in history, often for terrible reasons.
sentences.zh: 但我的意思是，历史上的重大事件往往都是因为可怕的原因才让人铭记。

sentences.en: They are, aren't they?
sentences.zh: 确实如此，不是吗？

sentences.en: So we've had murders and coups and enslavement and all kinds of horrors.
sentences.zh: 所以我们经历过谋杀、政变、奴役和各种各样的恐怖事件。

sentences.en: And more fun and jollity after the break.
sentences.zh: 中场休息之后会有更多欢乐和趣味。

sentences.en: Hello.
sentences.zh: 大家好。

sentences.en: Welcome back to The Rest of History, the 4th of January.
sentences.zh: 欢迎回到《余下历史》，今天是1月4日。

sentences.en: And Dominic, you're going to cheer us up by giving your choice for something that happened on this day.
sentences.zh: 多米尼克，你来讲讲今天发生的某件事来让我们高兴高兴吧。

sentences.en: So it is the 4th of January.
sentences.zh: 所以今天是1月4日。

sentences.en: We're in 1960.
sentences.zh: 时间是1960年。

sentences.en: Albert Camus, the French writer, has just been spending New Year in the south of France at his home in the Vaucluse in a village called Lomarin,
sentences.zh: 法国作家阿尔贝·加缪刚刚在法国南部沃克吕兹省洛马兰村的家中度过了新年，

sentences.en: which I've been to a very pretty sort of Provençal kind of village.
sentences.zh: 我去过那里，那是一个非常漂亮的普罗旺斯风格的小村庄。

sentences.en: Because, Tom, did you know that I spent a year living in Provence?
sentences.zh: 因为，汤姆，你知道我在普罗旺斯生活过一年吗？

sentences.en: I did.
sentences.zh: 我确实住过。

sentences.en: Peter Mayle style.
sentences.zh: 彼得·梅尔式的。

sentences.en: Yes, I did.
sentences.zh: 是的，我住过。

sentences.en: You were teaching, weren't you?
sentences.zh: 你当时在教书，对吧？

sentences.en: Yeah, I was teaching.
sentences.zh: 对，我在教书。

sentences.en: I was awful.
sentences.zh: 我糟透了。

sentences.en: I was totally out of my depth.
sentences.zh: 我完全应付不来。

sentences.en: You were wonderful.
sentences.zh: 你当时很棒。

sentences.en: No, I was terrible.
sentences.zh: 不，我太糟糕了。

sentences.en: Because they gave you no...
sentences.zh: 因为他们根本不给你……

sentences.en: Introducing Les Etudions to...
sentences.zh: 向学生们介绍……

sentences.en: It was awful, Tom.
sentences.zh: 太糟糕了，汤姆。

sentences.en: My French was so...
sentences.zh: 我的法语是那么……

sentences.en: British bacon and eggs.
sentences.zh: 英国培根和鸡蛋。

sentences.en: So I'd sort of thought, oh, I'm terribly good at French.
sentences.zh: 所以我当时想，哦，我法语好得不得了。

sentences.en: This will be an absolute triumph.
sentences.zh: 这绝对会是一场大获全胜。

sentences.en: And I arrived in France at the age of 21.
sentences.zh: 我21岁时来到了法国。

sentences.en: And I remember going to try and open my bank account so that I could receive my minimum wage from the French government.
sentences.zh: 我记得我去银行试图开个账户，好领取法国政府发放的最低工资。

sentences.en: And I stood there in front of this bank manager and I realised I didn't know how to say, I'd like to open my bank account.
sentences.zh: 我站在那个银行经理面前，却发现自己居然不知道怎么说“我想开个银行账户”。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是啊。

sentences.en: Because all I'd done is, you know, I'd been doing French literature.
sentences.zh: 因为我以前做过的，你知道的，我一直在研究法国文学。

sentences.en: So I knew how to say, what do you think about...
sentences.zh: 所以我只知道怎么说“你觉得……怎么样”

sentences.en: Madame Bovary is unhappy.
sentences.zh: 《包法利夫人》很不开心。

sentences.en: Yeah, Madame Bovary.
sentences.zh: 对，包法利夫人。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: But I was utterly out of my depth.
sentences.zh: 但我完全应付不来。

sentences.en: I can remember some people, the students used to say to me, you speak quite good French, but why do you speak it with that ludicrous comic English accent?
sentences.zh: 我记得有些人，那些学生曾经对我说，你法语说得挺好，但为什么非要带着那种荒谬可笑的英国腔呢？

sentences.en: Which I found very insulting.
sentences.zh: 我觉得这非常侮辱人。

sentences.en: Anyway, so Lourmarin, its claim to fame is that this was the home of the writer Albert Camus.
sentences.zh: 总之，洛马兰，它出名的原因在于这里曾是作家阿尔贝·加缪的居所。

sentences.en: And Camus, of course, is the sort of...
sentences.zh: 而加缪，当然了，他有点……

sentences.en: He's a little bit...
sentences.zh: 他有点……

sentences.en: I don't want to damn him, but he's the teenager's favourite, isn't he?
sentences.zh: 我不是想贬低他，但他可是青少年的最爱，对吧？

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是啊。

sentences.en: He looks very cool with a cigarette.
sentences.zh: 他叼着烟的样子看起来酷极了。

sentences.en: He looks terribly cool with a cigarette.
sentences.zh: 他叼着烟看起来酷毙了。

sentences.en: His book's about existentialism and so on.
sentences.zh: 他的书是关于存在主义之类的。

sentences.en: Although he never defined himself as an existentialist, did he?
sentences.zh: 尽管他从未把自己定义为存在主义者，对吧？

sentences.en: No, he didn't.
sentences.zh: 对，他没有。

sentences.en: He was an absurdiSt.
sentences.zh: 他是个荒诞主义者。

sentences.en: Yeah, exactly.
sentences.zh: 对，完全正确。

sentences.en: And actually, you know what?
sentences.zh: 说真的，你知道吗？

sentences.en: Particularly when the pandemic hit, lots of people went back to their copies of La Peste, The Plague, and they said, oh gosh, this is actually, you know, it's a genuinely,
sentences.zh: 尤其是在大流行爆发时，许多人重新翻开了《鼠疫》，他们说，天哪，这其实，你知道的，这是一本真正意义上的，

sentences.en: it's a really, really good book.
sentences.zh: 一本非常非常好的书。

sentences.en: And the fact that you read it when you were 18 and you thought it changed your...
sentences.zh: 你18岁时读过它，并觉得它改变了你的……

sentences.en: I mean, that's no reason to sort of curl your lip at it.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，这可不是对它撇嘴不屑的理由。

sentences.en: Yeah, well, I feel a bit the same about Nietzsche, to be honeSt.
sentences.zh: 好吧，老实说，我对尼采也有点这种感觉。

sentences.en: Really?
sentences.zh: 真的吗？

sentences.en: I've never heard Nietzsche.
sentences.zh: 我从没听过你提尼采。

sentences.en: I was absolutely mad for Nietzsche when I was 18.
sentences.zh: 我18岁时对尼采迷得发狂。

sentences.en: And then I kind of thought, oh, I've grown out of that.
sentences.zh: 然后我突然觉得，哦，我已经过了那个年纪了。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是啊。

sentences.en: And now I just thought, he's brilliant.
sentences.zh: 现在我又觉得，他太才华横溢了。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 对啊。

sentences.en: So maybe I should go back to Camus as well.
sentences.zh: 所以也许我也该重新去读读加缪。

sentences.en: That's sort of what I think about Camus, actually, because Camus was, I think, genuinely a very impressive man, much more impressive than Jean-Paul Sartre,
sentences.zh: 其实我就是这么看加缪的，因为加缪真的非常了不起，比让-保罗·萨特要强得多，

sentences.en: who's a terrible man by comparison.
sentences.zh: 相比之下萨特是个糟糕的家伙。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 对。

sentences.en: So Camus, he's born in Algeria, and he wrestles all his life with the fact that he's the product of a kind of French pied-noir, a settler family in Algeria.
sentences.zh: 所以加缪，他出生在阿尔及利亚，他一生都在与自己的出身搏斗——他是阿尔及利亚法国黑脚移民家庭的一员。

sentences.en: So he was neutral in the Algerian war, wasn't he?
sentences.zh: 所以他在阿尔及利亚战争中保持中立，对吧？

sentences.en: He was.
sentences.zh: 他是的。

sentences.en: He was.
sentences.zh: 他确实如此。

sentences.en: And you can absolutely understand why a lot of his sort of lefty friends in France sort of thought terribly badly of him and disavowed him for this.
sentences.zh: 你完全可以理解为什么他在法国的许多左翼朋友会因此极其看不起他并与他划清界限。

sentences.en: But his attitude was, which was sort of understandable.
sentences.zh: 但他的态度是，这其实某种程度上也是可以理解的。

sentences.en: I mean, he had this famous line, I love justice, but I love my mother more, which was shocking to the kind of Sartre and tendency,
sentences.zh: 我是说，他有过那句名言：我热爱正义，但我更热爱我的母亲。这让萨特那一派的人大惊失色，

sentences.en: because they thought abstract nouns were far more important than people.
sentences.zh: 因为他们觉得抽象名词远比活生生的人重要得多。

sentences.en: Yes.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: It's kind of like, I hope I would have the courage to betray my country over my friend.
sentences.zh: 这就好比，我希望我有勇气为了朋友而背叛祖国。

sentences.en: Exactly.
sentences.zh: 完全正确。

sentences.en: Reversed.
sentences.zh: 反过来了。

sentences.en: So Camus, he has been on this kind of intellectual journey, so round about the Second World War and just after the war.
sentences.zh: 所以加缪，他经历过这样一段知识分子心路历程，大约在第二次世界大战期间及战后不久。

sentences.en: And he has a good war, doesn't he?
sentences.zh: 而且他在战争期间表现很好，对吧？

sentences.en: I mean, he has a really good war.
sentences.zh: 我是说，他在战争期间表现真的非常出色。

sentences.en: So he edits Combat.
sentences.zh: 他担任了《战斗报》的主编。

sentences.en: Exactly.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: Which is a kind of resistance magazine.
sentences.zh: 那是一份抵抗运动的杂志。

sentences.en: I mean, he's incredibly brave.
sentences.zh: 我是说，他勇敢极了。

sentences.en: He's one of the sort of intellectual heroes of the resistance.
sentences.zh: 他是抵抗运动中的知识分子英雄之一。

sentences.en: And afterwards, like so many people in that milieu, he is, so he's this young, very sort of suave, but obviously Algerian, so he's got a bit of an outsider side to him.
sentences.zh: 战后，就像那个圈子里的许多人一样，他年轻、温文尔雅，但显然是阿尔及利亚人，所以他身上带有一种局外人的特质。

sentences.en: Very good footballer.
sentences.zh: 球踢得非常好。

sentences.en: Goalkeeper, wasn't he?
sentences.zh: 守门员，对吧？

sentences.en: Very good goalkeeper, yeah.
sentences.zh: 是个非常出色的守门员，对。

sentences.en: Where he played at university in Algiers.
sentences.zh: 他在阿尔及尔上大学时踢过球。

sentences.en: And he could have been really good, couldn't he?
sentences.zh: 他本来可以踢得很好的，不是吗？

sentences.en: He got some disease or something.
sentences.zh: 他得了某种病之类的。

sentences.en: Yeah, you never know whether these things are slightly exaggerated later because he's great.
sentences.zh: 对啊，你永远不知道这些事后人有没有添油加醋，因为他太棒了。

sentences.en: Like John Paul II.
sentences.zh: 就像保罗·约翰二世。

sentences.en: Yeah, exactly.
sentences.zh: 对，没错。

sentences.en: John Paul II, who almost played in goal for Real Madrid or something, if you just believe some accounts.
sentences.zh: 约翰·保罗二世，如果你相信某些说法的话，他差点给皇家马德里或者别的什么球队当守门员。

sentences.en: But actually probably just played, you know, goal twice or something.
sentences.zh: 但实际上可能也就是踢过，你知道，守过两次门什么的。

sentences.en: Anyway, Camus, he's always a bit of an outsider.
sentences.zh: 不管怎样，加缪，他总是有点局外人的感觉。

sentences.en: He never quite fits in.
sentences.zh: 他从来都无法真正融入。

sentences.en: And there's this period in the sort of late 40s where basically if you're a left-bank intellectual, you're very self-consciously left-wing.
sentences.zh: 在40年代末的那个时期，基本上只要你是左岸知识分子，你就会非常有意识地倾向左翼。

sentences.en: And pro-Stalin.
sentences.zh: 并且亲斯大林。

sentences.en: Pro-Stalin.
sentences.zh: 亲斯大林。

sentences.en: Camus, some people say he's a bit more of an anarchist than a communist, but certainly by the 50s, he is moving quite strongly in some ways to the centre.
sentences.zh: 加缪，有人说他比起共产主义者更像个无政府主义者，但毫无疑问到了50年代，他在某些方面相当强烈地向中间派靠拢。

sentences.en: You know, he's saying things like, you know, revolutionary violence is not a good thing.
sentences.zh: 你知道的，他会说出诸如革命暴力并非好事之类的话。

sentences.en: So he's kind of the French George Orwell.
sentences.zh: 所以他某种程度上就是法国的乔治·奥威尔。

sentences.en: Yeah, he is exactly.
sentences.zh: 对，他确实是。

sentences.en: He is exactly.
sentences.zh: 他确实是。

sentences.en: I mean, there's lots of differences, so it's not an exact parallel.
sentences.zh: 我是说，这有很大不同，所以并不是完全对等。

sentences.en: But you're absolutely right that he occupies that place of being the sort of left-wing with a tremendous backstory like Orwell.
sentences.zh: 但你绝对说得对，他占据了那个位置，就像奥威尔一样，是一个有着极其丰富背景故事的左翼人士。

sentences.en: Very opposed to Stalinism.
sentences.zh: 非常反对斯大林主义。

sentences.en: Very opposed to Stalinism and increasingly sort of interested in human detail, I suppose, and the texture of ordinary people's lives rather than grand ideological schemes.
sentences.zh: 非常反对斯大林主义，而且我猜，他越来越对人类的细节感兴趣，比起宏大的意识形态蓝图，他更关注普通人生活的质感。

sentences.en: Abstractions.
sentences.zh: 那些抽象的概念。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 对。

sentences.en: So he's been given the Nobel Prize, which people see as, they see that as a Cold War thing, you know, as almost encouraging him to back towards the centre.
sentences.zh: 所以他被授予了诺贝尔奖，人们认为这带有冷战色彩，你知道的，几乎是在鼓励他退回中间立场。

sentences.en: There's a bit of a slap in the face.
sentences.zh: 这有点像打脸。

sentences.en: Well, because you know the only person younger than him to get the Nobel Prize.
sentences.zh: 嗯，因为你知道获得诺贝尔奖比他年轻的只有一个人。

sentences.en: Oh, that's a good one.
sentences.zh: 哦，这个有意思。

sentences.en: I knew he was one of the youngeSt.
sentences.zh: 我知道他是最年轻的几个人之一。

sentences.en: He was the second youngeSt.
sentences.zh: 他是第二年轻的。

sentences.en: Who's the youngest youngest?
sentences.zh: 谁是最年轻的那个？

sentences.en: Kipling.
sentences.zh: 吉卜林。

sentences.en: I was about to say Kipling.
sentences.zh: 我正要说是吉卜林。

sentences.en: So Kipling must have got it very early then.
sentences.zh: 那吉卜林一定很早就获奖了。

sentences.en: Kipling got it really early, yeah.
sentences.zh: 吉卜林确实很早就拿奖了，对。

sentences.en: But then Camus is the second youngeSt.
sentences.zh: 但加缪是第二年轻的。

sentences.en: Two top writers.
sentences.zh: 两位顶尖作家。

sentences.en: I'm very pleased to see them.
sentences.zh: 我很高兴看到他们。

sentences.en: I don't imagine they'd have got on, though, do you?
sentences.zh: 不过我想他们应该合不来吧？

sentences.en: No.
sentences.zh: 不会的。

sentences.en: Kipling and Camus?
sentences.zh: 吉卜林和加缪？

sentences.en: No.
sentences.zh: 不会的。

sentences.en: Kipling would have had no time for Camus.
sentences.zh: 吉卜林根本不会理睬加缪。

sentences.en: No.
sentences.zh: 不会的。

sentences.en: All that sort of smoking and lounging around in cafes.
sentences.zh: 那种抽烟和在咖啡馆闲逛的作风。

sentences.en: Kipling would have been off on, you know, doing bushcraft or something.
sentences.zh: 吉卜林早就跑到野外去搞什么丛林生存训练了。

sentences.en: Anyway, so Camus, he's not terribly happy, I think, at the end of the 1950s, although he's got his Nobel Prize.
sentences.zh: 不管怎样，所以加缪，我想他在20世纪50年代末并不是特别快乐，尽管他拿到了诺贝尔奖。

sentences.en: For some people in the sort of old intellectual establishment, he's a bit persona non grata.
sentences.zh: 在某些老派知识分子阶层看来，他有点像是不受欢迎的人。

sentences.en: So he's been down at his house in the south for New Year with his family and with his publisher, who's a man called Michel Gallimard.
sentences.zh: 所以他带着家人和出版商米歇尔·加利马尔去他在南方的宅邸过年。

sentences.en: Camus and Gallimard's wife and daughter.
sentences.zh: 加缪还有加利马尔的妻子和女儿。

sentences.en: And they decide they're going to go back to Paris.
sentences.zh: 他们决定回巴黎。

sentences.en: So on the 2nd of January, Camus' wife and children go off back to Paris on by train.
sentences.zh: 所以在1月2日，加缪的妻子和孩子坐火车回巴黎。

sentences.en: And Gallimard says to Camus, well, I'll give you a lift.
sentences.zh: 加利马尔对加缪说，我载你一程吧。

sentences.en: Stay another couple of days and I'll give you a lift in my very fancy car.
sentences.zh: 再待几天，我用我那辆非常豪华的车载你。

sentences.en: Camus, yeah, tremendous.
sentences.zh: 加缪说，好啊，太棒了。

sentences.en: So on the 4th of January, they set off.
sentences.zh: 所以在1月4日，他们出发了。

sentences.en: And basically, no one really knows what happens.
sentences.zh: 基本上，没有人真正知道发生了什么。

sentences.en: But they're not that far from Paris.
sentences.zh: 但他们离巴黎其实不远。

sentences.en: And when the car goes off the road and hits a plane tree and Gallimard's wife and daughter escape unscathed, Camus is killed instantaneously and Gallimard dies a few days later.
sentences.zh: 当汽车冲出路面撞上一棵法国梧桐树时，加利马尔的妻子和女儿安然无恙，加缪当场身亡，加利马尔几天后也去世了。

sentences.en: So, and in the car is the 144-page manuscript of what Camus has written so far, the novel that he thinks will be his masterpiece, which is called Le Premier Homme, The First Man.
sentences.zh: 所以，车里还有加缪当时写到一半、长达144页的手稿，也就是他认为会成为自己巅峰之作的小说，名叫《第一人》，英文是The First Man。

sentences.en: And this is going to be his first really autobiographical novel about growing up in Algeria.
sentences.zh: 这将是他第一部真正具有自传性质的小说，讲述在阿尔及利亚的成长经历。

sentences.en: So a very profound kind of subject, given that the Franco-Algerian war is absolutely in full swing.
sentences.zh: 考虑到阿尔及利亚战争正打得火热，这是一个非常深刻的主题。

sentences.en: And he's going to be writing quite lyrically about the experience of growing up in Algeria.
sentences.zh: 他将用极具诗意的笔触描写在阿尔及利亚成长的经历。

sentences.en: And of course, that book is never finished, isn't published until I think something like 30 years later.
sentences.zh: 当然，那本书永远没有完成，直到我想大概30年后才出版。

sentences.en: Camus killed.
sentences.zh: 加缪遇难。

sentences.en: And at the time, lots of people say it must be a conspiracy.
sentences.zh: 当时，很多人说这一定是一场阴谋。

sentences.en: He must have been murdered by the KGB because of his move back towards the kind of political center.
sentences.zh: 他一定是因为向政治中间立场靠拢而被克格勃暗杀了。

sentences.en: But almost certainly, that's not the case.
sentences.zh: 但几乎可以肯定，事实并非如此。

sentences.en: It's just sort of Gallimard's bad driving or whatever.
sentences.zh: 这只是加利马尔车技太差或者类似的原因。

sentences.en: I mean, who knows?
sentences.zh: 我是说，谁知道呢？

sentences.en: Not Prince Philip.
sentences.zh: 不是菲利普亲王。

sentences.en: No.
sentences.zh: 不是。

sentences.en: Well, Prince Philip obviously has form with Gallic car crashes.
sentences.zh: 好吧，菲利普亲王显然有制造法国车祸的前科。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 对。

sentences.en: But in this case, no, he wasn't involved at all, as far as I know.
sentences.zh: 但在这种情况下，据我所知，他绝对没有参与。

sentences.en: So I studied for French at school, a play by Camus called Les Justes.
sentences.zh: 所以我上学时学过法语，读过加缪的一部戏剧叫《正义者》。

sentences.en: Oh, yeah.
sentences.zh: 哦，对。

sentences.en: I remember Les Justes.
sentences.zh: 我记得《正义者》。

sentences.en: Revolutionaries, Russian revolutionaries.
sentences.zh: 革命者，俄国革命者。

sentences.en: Yes.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: And the plot of that, they have to blow up a Russian prince or something in a car.
sentences.zh: 那部剧的剧情是，他们必须在车里炸死一个俄国亲王什么的。

sentences.en: That's it.
sentences.zh: 就是这样。

sentences.en: In a carriage.
sentences.zh: 是在马车里。

sentences.en: So kind of death on roads is an eerie prefiguring.
sentences.zh: 所以这种公路死亡真是一种诡异的预兆。

sentences.en: And he wrote a play about Caligula.
sentences.zh: 他还写过一部关于卡利古拉的戏剧。

sentences.en: He did, yeah.
sentences.zh: 他写过，是的。

sentences.en: Which I remember doing at A-level.
sentences.zh: 我记得我A-level考试时学过。

sentences.en: And it ends, Caligula was killed.
sentences.zh: 结局是，卡利古拉被杀了。

sentences.en: And the last line is, he shouts, I'm still alive, as he's been killed.
sentences.zh: 最后一句话是，他在被杀时大喊“我还活着”。

sentences.en: And then the play ends.
sentences.zh: 然后戏剧结束。

sentences.en: Very profound.
sentences.zh: 非常深刻。

sentences.en: I have to say, I find all those 50s French plays, which I studied a lot, I find them terrible.
sentences.zh: 我必须说，我发现所有那些我学过很多的50年代法国戏剧简直糟糕透顶。

sentences.en: And indeed acted in.
sentences.zh: 而且我还演过。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 对。

sentences.en: Well, there's Jean Anouis.
sentences.zh: 还有让·安努伊的作品。

sentences.en: I mean, I'm always happy to mention that on the, I think the listeners have probably heard enough about that for the time being.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，我总是很乐意在节目里提这个，我想听众们对此大概已经听够了。

sentences.en: But I think they're just, so all those Sartre plays, Les Mansales and stuff, Dirty Hands, they're basically people just standing and talking to each other endlessly.
sentences.zh: 但我觉得它们就是，所有那些萨特的戏剧，比如《死无葬身之地》之类的，《脏手》，基本上就是人们站在那里没完没了地对话。

sentences.en: What is violence?
sentences.zh: 什么是暴力？

sentences.en: You know, all this, they're dramatically, utterly inert, I think.
sentences.zh: 你知道，诸如此类，它们在戏剧性上简直毫无生气，我认为。

sentences.en: But I think Camus' novels, and he wrote a- And the myth of Sisyphus.
sentences.zh: 但我觉得加缪的小说，他写过——还有《西西弗神话》。

sentences.en: Yes.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: One must think that Sisyphus is happy.
sentences.zh: 人们必须想象西西弗斯是快乐的。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 对。

sentences.en: I mean, that's a kind of memorable tagline.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，这是一个令人难忘的金句。

sentences.en: Yeah, it's a good image.
sentences.zh: 对，这是一个很好的意象。

sentences.en: It's a, I mean, that's his sort of statement of the absurd, isn't it?
sentences.zh: 这是一个，我的意思是，这是他对荒诞的宣言，对吧？

sentences.en: He also wrote some very interesting short stories called Exile in the Kingdom.
sentences.zh: 他还写过一些非常有趣短篇小说集叫《流放与王国》。

sentences.en: A lot of them set in Algeria, which are kind of quite weird.
sentences.zh: 其中很多故事以阿尔及利亚为背景，都相当诡异。

sentences.en: And they've been attacked by critics as a bit orientalizing.
sentences.zh: 它们曾被评论家攻击为有点东方主义色彩。

sentences.en: But that's kind of inevitable, I suppose, if you're growing up as part of that sort of settler community surrounded by, you know, North African MusliMs.
sentences.zh: 但我想这也是难免的，如果你作为一个定居者群体长大，周围都是北非穆斯林的话。

sentences.en: You know what, the very first piece of research I ever did, Tom, was on French colonial Algeria.
sentences.zh: 你知道吗，汤姆，我做过的第一项研究就是关于法属殖民地阿尔及利亚的。

sentences.en: Yes, you've mentioned this.
sentences.zh: 是的，你提过这个。

sentences.en: You have mentioned this.
sentences.zh: 你提过这个。

sentences.en: A pogrom in the city of Constantine in 1934.
sentences.zh: 1934年君士坦丁市的大屠杀。

sentences.en: And, well, we're going to do it.
sentences.zh: 而且，我们打算讲讲这个。

sentences.en: We're going to do the Algerian War.
sentences.zh: 我们要讲阿尔及利亚战争。

sentences.en: That'd be a great subject.
sentences.zh: 那会是个很棒的主题。

sentences.en: It's really fascinating.
sentences.zh: 真的非常引人入胜。

sentences.en: And, of course, people who came to our live show will know we are great fans of the Battle of Algiers.
sentences.zh: 当然，来我们现场秀的人都知道我们是《阿尔及利亚之战》的超级粉丝。

sentences.en: So lots to look forward to on that front.
sentences.zh: 所以这方面有很多值得期待的内容。

sentences.en: We've got more Gaelic conduct tomorrow, actually.
sentences.zh: 事实上，我们明天还有更多关于高卢内容的节目。

sentences.en: Yes, we have.
sentences.zh: 是的，我们有。

sentences.en: Yes.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: And a stunning rebuke for people who've sometimes said there's not enough French history on this podcaSt.
sentences.zh: 对于那些有时抱怨这个播客里法国历史不够多的人来说，这是一个响亮的耳光。

sentences.en: We're absolutely wallowing in French history.
sentences.zh: 我们完全沉浸在法国历史中。

sentences.en: Yeah, we've actually got two French-themed topics tomorrow, but we mustn't reveal what they are.
sentences.zh: 对，我们明天实际上有两个以法国为主题的话题，但我们不能透露它们是什么。

sentences.en: We must leave the tension cranked up.
sentences.zh: 我们必须保持悬念。

sentences.en: But tomorrow is obviously the most important day of the year, 5th of January, because it's my birthday.
sentences.zh: 但明天显然是一年中最重要的日子，1月5日，因为是我的生日。

sentences.en: Tom Holland's birthday.
sentences.zh: 汤姆·霍兰的生日。

sentences.en: What a great moment.
sentences.zh: 多么美好的时刻。

sentences.en: So, of course, it's not.
sentences.zh: 所以，当然不是。

sentences.en: You get two birthdays, don't you?
sentences.zh: 你其实有两个生日，对吧？

sentences.en: You're like the Queen, because you have your real birthday, and then you have your official Twitter birthday, where people, teenagers in America...
sentences.zh: 你就像女王一样，因为你有真正的生日，然后你还有官方的推特生日，美国的青少年们会在那一天……

sentences.en: Yes, probably.
sentences.zh: 是的，大概吧。

sentences.en: ...send you...
sentences.zh: ……发信息给你……

sentences.en: Tell them that they want to marry me, which is lovely.
sentences.zh: 告诉他们想嫁给我，这很可爱。

sentences.en: You know, though Sadie doesn't really...
sentences.zh: 你知道的，虽然萨迪其实并不觉得……

sentences.en: It always comes as a shock to her when she finds it.
sentences.zh: 她每次发现这些时总是感到震惊。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 对。

sentences.en: What are all these messages from people...
sentences.zh: 这些都是谁发的消息……

sentences.en: 22-year-old in Rio de Janeiro is offering herself to me.
sentences.zh: 里约热内卢的22岁姑娘向我表白。

sentences.en: I just can't be saying no.
sentences.zh: 我实在无法拒绝。

sentences.en: None of that nonsense.
sentences.zh: 没有那种废话。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 对。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 好啦。

sentences.en: We'll see you tomorrow.
sentences.zh: 我们明天见。

sentences.en: Goodbye.
sentences.zh: 再见。

sentences.en: Bye-bye.
sentences.zh: 拜拜。

sentences.en: Thanks for listening to The Rest is History.
sentences.zh: 感谢收听《历史的余烬》。

sentences.zh: 如需获取独家单集、抢先收听、无广告体验以及我们的聊天社区权限，请在 restishistorypod.com 注册。

sentences.zh: That's restishistorypod.com.
